Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

agree verb

with someone

also I agree, be of the same opinion, agreement, in agreement, by common agreement

classical

Cic. de Or. 1.126: valdē tibi adsentior
Traupman 177: nōluī prōpalam assentīrī Crassō

assentior, assentīrī, assēnsus sum

verb, fourth conjugation, deponent, with the dative

agree with (a person, a view)

Often printed adsentior. Assentior on its own is “I agree”. The active assentiō is rare: Plautus, Vergil, and three times in Cicero’s letters (Lewis & Short).

Other words

  • cōnsentiō, cōnsentīre, cōnsēnsī, cōnsēnsum — agree, be of one mind (cum aliquō, dē rē)

    verb, fourth conjugation · also used · classical · Cic. Lael. 86: dē amīcitiae ūtilitāte omnēs ūnō ōre cōnsentiunt (Lewis & Short); Traupman 148, 270

  • cōnsēnsus, cōnsēnsūs m. — agreement, unanimity

    noun, fourth declension · also used · classical · Cic. Tusc. 1.35: omnium cōnsēnsus nātūrae vōx est (Lewis & Short); Caes. BG 1.30: ex commūnī cōnsēnsū (Lewis & Short)

    By common agreement, commūnī cōnsēnsū.

  • dissentiō, dissentīre, dissēnsī, dissēnsum — disagree (ā + ablative)

    verb, fourth conjugation · also used · classical · Cic. de Or. 1.5: solēsque nōn numquam hāc dē rē ā mē in disputātiōnibus nostrīs dissentīre; Traupman 96: vehementer ā tē dissentiō

Examples

  • illud vērō quod ā tē dictum est … valdē tibi adsentior

    but what you said … I entirely agree withCic. de Or. 1.126

  • Dē eā rē tēcum funditus cōnsentiō.

    I agree with you completely on that point.Traupman 148

See also agree, that’s right, you’re right.
